rubric.description: Defines metabolism as the sum total of chemical reactions in an organism.
rubric.how: Check that the answer identifies metabolism as the combined chemical reactions taking place in a living organism.

rubric.description: Names Theodor Schwann as the person who first used the term or gave the concept of metabolism.
rubric.how: Check for the name Theodor Schwann.

modelAnswer: Metabolism is the sum total of all chemical reactions taking place in a living organism.
The term metabolism was first used by Theodor Schwann in 1839.

items.followUp: Write the word equation for photosynthesis and name the conditions it requires.

rubric.why: Awards the correct reactants and products.
rubric.description: Identifies carbon dioxide and water as reactants, and glucose and oxygen as products.
rubric.how: Check for all four substances in the correct roles.

rubric.why: Awards the balanced equation for photosynthesis.
rubric.how: Check that the equation shows six carbon dioxide and six water molecules forming glucose and six oxygen molecules.

modelAnswer: Photosynthesis is the process by which green plants use light energy to make glucose from carbon dioxide and water, releasing oxygen.
6CO₂ + 6H₂O → C₆H₁₂O₆ + 6O₂ (in the presence of light and chlorophyll).

items.followUp: What is the role of ATP in cellular activities?

rubric.why: Awards the name of the discoverer.
rubric.description: Names Karl Lohmann as the discoverer of ATP.
rubric.how: Check for the name Karl Lohmann.

rubric.description: Gives 1929 as the year ATP was discovered.

modelAnswer: ATP was discovered by Karl Lohmann.

items.followUp: Where does glycolysis occur, and what is its main product?

rubric.why: Awards the central change in glycolysis.
rubric.description: States that glucose is broken down to pyruvic acid (pyruvate).
rubric.how: Check for glucose as the starting molecule and pyruvic acid or pyruvate as the product.

rubric.why: Awards the cellular location of glycolysis.
rubric.description: States that glycolysis occurs in the cytoplasm.

modelAnswer: Glycolysis is the series of reactions in which one glucose molecule is broken down into two molecules of pyruvic acid.
It takes place in the cytoplasm of the cell.

items.followUp: Explain how cohesion between water molecules helps water move upward through xylem.

rubric.why: Awards the cause that initiates the pull.
rubric.description: Explains that water loss from leaves by transpiration creates tension or suction in the xylem.
rubric.how: Check for transpiration or evaporation from leaves as the cause of the pull.

rubric.why: Awards the properties that help transmit the pull.
rubric.description: Explains that cohesion between water molecules, aided by adhesion to xylem walls, maintains a continuous water column and transmits the pull.
rubric.how: Check for cohesion between water molecules or adhesion to xylem walls.

modelAnswer: Evaporation of water from leaf surfaces during transpiration creates tension (suction) in the xylem.
Cohesion between water molecules, aided by their adhesion to xylem walls, keeps the water column continuous so the pull is transmitted upward.

items.followUp: Name the main components of the human circulatory system.

rubric.why: Awards identification of one transport system in humans.
rubric.how: Check for circulatory system or cardiovascular system.

rubric.why: Awards identification of the other transport system.

modelAnswer: The circulatory system and the lymphatic system are responsible for transport in humans.

items.followUp: Name the two main types of white blood cells and give one example of each.

rubric.why: Awards one main classification of white blood cells.
rubric.description: Names granulocytes as one main type of white blood cell.

rubric.why: Awards the other main classification of white blood cells.
rubric.description: Names agranulocytes as the other main type of white blood cell.

modelAnswer: The two main types of white blood cells are granulocytes and agranulocytes.

items.followUp: Explain how biology is related to chemistry and physics through interdisciplinary sciences.

rubric.why: Awards the central idea that biology is connected with other sciences.
rubric.description: Explains that combining biology with other sciences creates interdisciplinary fields.
rubric.how: Check that the answer states a connection between biology and other sciences.

rubric.why: Awards the relationship between biology and physics.
rubric.description: Defines biophysics as applying physics to biological phenomena.
rubric.how: Check for biophysics and its link to physics or biological phenomena.

rubric.why: Awards the relationship between biology and chemistry.
rubric.description: Defines biochemistry as the study of chemicals and chemical processes in living organisms.
rubric.how: Check for biochemistry and its link to chemistry or chemical processes in living organisms.

rubric.why: Awards a valid mathematical or statistical interdisciplinary field.
rubric.description: Identifies biometry, biostatistics, or biomathematics as applying mathematics or statistics to biological data.
rubric.how: Check for one of these fields and its mathematical or statistical role.

rubric.why: Awards another valid interdisciplinary field and its relationship to biology.
rubric.description: Describes bioinformatics, biogeography, or bioeconomics and the related subject it combines with biology.
rubric.how: Check for a valid field paired with its connection to computer science, geographical distribution, or economics.

modelAnswer: Biology is linked with other sciences, producing interdisciplinary fields that combine methods and knowledge from both subjects.
Biophysics applies the principles of physics to biological phenomena.
Biochemistry studies the chemicals and chemical processes in living organisms.
Biometry or biostatistics uses mathematical and statistical methods to analyse biological data.
Bioinformatics applies computer science to biological information; biogeography studies the geographical distribution of organisms.
